speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In any society, Youth is a demographic of significance.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Various authorities define this group differently but suffice to say that the period of youth generally starts at the cusp of late adolescence, into the years of formal adulthood and transits to the early working life of an adult.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is the energy and gumption, the health and verve, as well as the innovation and pushing of boundaries by youths that are key to propel any society forward to the next bound.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Youths are foundation and key to a society’s future survival.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Where leaders can dream, where governments can plan and policies implemented, the longer-term sustainability of such an effort will eventually fall squarely on the shoulders of youths of today, for they are the leaders of tomorrow.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It must be the case that they remain rightly invested and guided in principles and values, as well as have the right capability and skills in leadership to keep society cohesive and Singapore successful.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is also from the churning belly and energy of youths that economies thrive, productivity is at its firm best and the fire of entrepreneurship lights new opportunities and growth for the country.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Youths are both the agents of social change, yet also the conduit of cultural continuity.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: They sometimes challenge established social norms, question the relevance of certain rules and whether some things remain important or should change.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The sustenance of any language, culture, heritage and values anchor on its acceptance and willingness for active participation of youths as their torchbearers into the future, else they will vanish and left only to be admired and talked about in museums rather than lived by.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Youths, Mr Speaker, are also society’s bulwark of resilience and recovery from challenges and adversity.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: How a society develops its youths, the indicators of their growth, their outlook, their worldview and their ability to adapt are forward indicators of how youth as a group can weather storms, crises and turbulent times for themselves and for the country in future.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: How youths manage stressors today, would be a reasonable indicator of how the country manages a crisis tomorrow.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: How adaptable and resilient our youths are today, would be a fair measure of how the country and society tolerates uncertainty tomorrow.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If we err in developing our youths, the country suffers tomorrow.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We must endeavour to get it right and we must give every opportunity for our youth to thrive.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: For our youths to thrive, it must be that they are energetic, enthusiastic and optimistic about future paths of success; that there is scope for them to believe deeply that they can realise their potential to flourish, to grow and to be better versions of themselves.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: They must be able to find themselves in networks of trust, safety and support, enough for them to feel confident to push boundaries, to move out of their comfort zone and to take on a growth mindset.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: They must feel ready to express and stand by their views for a better world for the future of their generation, yet still be prepared to stand corrected and be open to opposing ideas.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There must also be a willingness to think beyond themselves and consider wider societal mores, be forgiving of setbacks and kind to well-intended failures, yet still maintain the resilience, ruggedness and fervour to go at it again and again and again.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: How then do we build a youth core that is fiercely competitive, skilled, passionate and spirited when it needs to be, yet at the same time, tampering with traits of compassion, a sense of community and togetherness, mutual respect and dignity for ourselves and one another?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: First, to redefine what success means for youths.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Third, to give opportunity for youths to express their views.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: And fourth, to ensure our youths continue to have a strong sense of rootedness to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: That there should be space for "U-turns, side steps, slowdowns, pauses, experimentation and outliers", and to "respect all forms of work and never be afraid to try".

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In the Prime Minister's words, "no need to squeeze ourselves into boxes we were never meant to fit".

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In gist, I agree with the hon Prime Minister's view of redefining success.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There is so much more that life has to offer and I have some confidence that the youths resonate with that; where there must be a plethora of pathways to find meaning and purpose in our lives as Singaporeans and our yardstick of success in life must widen beyond material gains.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The sustainability of this cultural and mindset shift on redefining success will hinge on the lived experience of ordinary youths and whether their families view this with the same enthusiasm or scepticism, especially from families of less privilege; one with no safety net materially or for those who have only one shot at success to uplift those around him or her, where pauses and U-turns, perhaps cost a lot more in relative terms for themselves and their families.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: For this redefinition to happen, and happen well, the effort to shift must not only be taken in our schools for our students and educators, but it must also permeate through the psyche of our businesses, employers, parents and even our scholarship panels who lend opportunity to youths who wish to pursue creative and less than traditional pathways of success.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If we want youthful innovation to thrive, their exuberance and passions to take flight, and also groom their willingness for U-turns, side steps and experimentation, then, as a society, some reassurance needs to be there, that it is okay to bruise once in a while, that it is okay to misstep and tumble, as long as there is safety net such that you are not falling the full flight of stairs and risking too much at a time of yourself and the needs of your family.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Emerging into the hallways of adulthood, or "adulting" as the youths say, our youths are restless about their futures, too.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Notwithstanding their idealism and passion, they take a pragmatic view of their circumstances in that their passions are not necessarily sacred cows, especially when balanced against the rising costs of living, the responsibility to put food on the table and the need to care for their families, dependants and children.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If we can provide assurance that there is value, that there is an amelioration of some risk and a provision of safety to explore beyond the traditional measures of success, it will go some way to pivot our youths to go into paths less travelled.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Second, on building confidence for our youths, I was struck by the recent findings of the 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment award by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) through the press release of the Ministry of Education on 18 June.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In another global study comparing global reading literacy levels in Primary 4 students, our students topped the Progress in International Literacy Study last year.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is not the case that I am advocating for us to toot our horns or be haughty about our achievements.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: To be hungry for more and not be blinded by success keeps us on our toes, and a good dose of humility keeps us grounded as a country, for there are other things we are deficient and needful of.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, there is scope for us to develop better confidence and optimism in our youths in their ability and standing in the world today and being raised from an education system that is world-class, by educators who care, and through a work ethic and culture that is resilient and robust.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Arguably, the early education indicators suggest that all things being equal, our youths can compete more widely against the world and will do well.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If we wish for our youths to thrive, an important part of this narrative must be that they, too, are able to value themselves in alignment with their abilities, that they are encouraged to stand and be counted as youths of potential, and that they are allowed to recognise and be excited about the prospect of success well beyond our shores and the global opportunities at their doorstep.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Only then will we be able to realise the full strength and potential of an education system we have invested so much in and restore the confidence, optimism and self-belief for our youths to thrive.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Our youths can take heart that they start from a position of strength and can rightly have some latitude to feel confident and be positive of their abilities, to not fret the small stuff and that they have it in themselves to be resilient in the face of any uncertainty that the world may bring.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Third, on giving opportunity for youths to express their views, we live in a world today that is so interconnected that it is impossible to ignore what happens around us, whether in our neighbourhoods, locally or from a place far away.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Our youths are digital natives and their calibration of social proximity, networks and friendships are not the same as the generations before.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: They devour news online, are open to the influences of the world and care about the happenings around them.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: They want to make a difference and be a helpful citizen of Singapore and also to the world.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Our youths are exposed to global trends and happenings very quickly and sometimes graphically so.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: They have views, some stronger and more passionate than others, about many things, whether it be about climate change and environmental concerns, wars raging and people needlessly dying around the world, as well as strong views on issues relating to inequality, mental well-being, the construct of family and sexuality, drug habits and intergenerational differences.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If we want our youths to thrive, for them to be raised with a global outlook and have a fire in the belly to think critically and creatively about the world around them, then it must come with a willingness for us to lend opportunity for them to express their thoughts and lend their voice as, together, we knit the social fabric that is Singapore.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: More so than having a seat at the table for youths to share their concerns as a member of society invested in our collective future, when youths express their views, it allows them a further exercise of having to know one another, to acknowledge diversity of worldviews, locally and overseas, and then further celebrate that diversity.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is also an exercise for our youths to develop skills for difficult conversations, to develop a readiness to be corrected and to appreciate that we all have our blind spots coming from our respective social, cultural and religious traditions.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is then incumbent on us to create spaces and allow platforms for youths to feel comfortable and confident in the expression of their views, whether they be in agreement and support, or disdain and frustration, over the status quo.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: As the world becomes more diverse, layered and complex, a youth core skilled in negotiating difficult decisions respectfully, interacting with differences of opinion calmly and achieving common intent pragmatically, will be a distinctive trait to a world becoming more and more polarised.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The world is getting smaller, the search for talent is stiff and our youths, too, are very much sought after and valued.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Youths are more mobile than the generations before, and we do want them to seize the opportunities globally and be well-travelled, but yet, still maintain strong ties and roots back home.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In this space, we must make an effort to build greater social connectedness, as well as civic participation and affiliation in our youths that stand the test of time and the allure of opportunities beyond our shores.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is less a question of dollars and cents, and more of how connected they are back to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We want them to see this red dot as a place to build families, raise children and as a safe and a secure place to live and play; for our youths to feel that this is the place that allows them to flourish and grow, for them to have confidence in our public institutions, and for them to care deeply about Singapore and that Singapore cares deeply for them as well.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This can only be had by a strengthening of national identity, collective experiences through school, work, National Service and a social connectedness to family, friends and the way of life here.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: These are things that are intangible, are less than formulaic, take decades to build and require a combined function of social policy, leadership and pragmatism that cut across all sectors, whether they be public, people or private sectors.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This also allows a virtuous cycle of thriving youths who turn into leaders of tomorrow who care for the country and then create opportunity for the society and youths of tomorrow to thrive in turn.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Today, it is anchored under the Ministry of Culture Community and Youth (MCCY), more specifically with the National Youth Council, and rightly so.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, in terms of actionable steps, the youth agenda could be palpable more widely.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It should percolate through to how we curate policy, with youths as an enabling consideration and part of the nation's sustainability plan for our future.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The firm anchor and starting point of youth development remains in terms of early accessibility to education, not just in terms of academics alone but also for the development of character, values and self-confidence, as well as starting all our children with the correct and equitable footing to begin their lives.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, beyond access to school and education, might we be able to consider other aspects of support and imagine different solutions that contribute to a thriving ecosystem for our youths?

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I would also like to acknowledge the many youth leaders who are here in the gallery today, in support of Dr Harun's important Adjournment Motion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last month, at the National Youth Council's Leaders Course, I met youth leaders Ernie, Kaegen and Danish.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They youth leaders shared with me about their experience in the National Youth Leaders Course, overcoming physical obstacles during the Outward Bound School (OBS) segment of the course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They were initially daunted by the physical challenges, but ultimately, through mentoring, coaching and the support of peers, they gained the confidence to overcome the physical, mental and emotional obstacles in their way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But we do not want to provide a fail-safe environment because that simply does not exist in the real world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Instead, the best thing we can do for our youths, is to equip them with the tools that they need to thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is exactly what we are doing and will continue doing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But beyond OBS, we also have other programmes and platforms to equip our youths to thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For youths who are adulting, we launched our national mentoring movement, Mentoring SG, in 2022 to create more mentoring opportunities to equip them with perspectives and opportunities from mentors, so they can chart and walk their own path.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Together with our youths, we launched Well-Being Circles under our SG Mental Well-Being Network to equip citizens, including youths, with the skills to care for themselves and those around them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Cho Ming Xiu, who leads Campus PSY, a member of the SG Mental Well-being Network is here today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Campus PSY is a ground-up youth organisation, working on youth mental well-being and peer support work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Then, as part of our Youth Action Challenge, beyond funding, we equip our youths with skills to develop sustainable business plans and they must in the Youth Action Challenge pitch their ideas to a panel.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, they will need help to learn how to pitch, how to negotiate and how to persuade a panel, which is very useful for them as they go out to the working world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through our Youth Panels, we are equipping them with tools to solve societal challenges of our day.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Some of our Youth Panels members are here today and they have been working closely with us on topics such as financial security, financial literacy, sustainability, evolving careers as well as digital well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Youth Panels will be sharing their preliminary ideas in the upcoming Youth Policy Forum in August.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Dr Harun also asked how we are working with other Ministries and partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Indeed, we are working with many of them, again, to equip our youths with the skills and the opportunities to thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Ministry of Manpower and National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) are key partners of the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth, and Mentoring SG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are working with our tripartite partners to onboard corporates to provide industry-relevant mentoring opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We work with, for example, NTUC's Youth Taskforce, which Member Desmond Choo has been leading.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, Young NTUC provides mentorships, internships, mental well-being support and its Career Starter Lab, which NTUC is championing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have also put together with our NTUC counterparts a strong line-up of over 100 corporates, including impressive names such as Micron, Timbre, CISCO, LinkedIn, JobStreet, Prudential, and also trade associations and chambers of commerce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example the Singapore Fintech Association, the Singapore Semiconductor Association, ST Aerospace Engineering and Singapore International Chambers of Commerce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, we are tying them with industries so that they have key industry perspectives and opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also partner the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Trade and Industry and Enterprise Singapore to equip our youths to be ready not just for the region but for the rest of the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, we have an Asia-Ready Exposure Programme which equips our youths to be Asia-Ready through exposure to ASEAN member states, China and India.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also have a Youth Leaders Exchange Programme with countries in the region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I was just with our youth leaders at the Second China-Singapore Youth Leader Campus in Singapore in April.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In fact, this month, our youths will be in China for the second leg of this programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This month also, it is going to be very busy for our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I am looking forward to working with the team on the Singapore-Malaysia Youth Leaders Exchange Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, we are expanding this space and our youths are out there interacting with their counterparts, learning from their counterparts and forming long-term networks with their counterparts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Its founder, Clarence Ching, is in the gallery today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He had just returned from a leadership camp in the United States (US).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: While he was there, we had been in touch on WhatsApp.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I was checking in on him and he was telling me what he had learnt in camp.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last night, he came by and he was very eager to share with me what he had learnt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He told me that he had gained valuable leadership experiences and valuable perspectives about the US and also about Singapore’s unique place in the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Tristan told me that his "American peers at camp regard Singapore very highly for our safety and success despite our size".

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Tristan came back feeling more inspired to serve and plant roots in Singapore – the rootedness point that Dr Harun had mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For youths like Tristan, we will continue to turn their aspirations to serve into actions to serve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In fact, Youth Corps Singapore celebrates its 10th year anniversary this Saturday.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Prime Minister Wong will be joining us at the Carnival at *SCAPE and I invite all Members to also join us to celebrate Youth Corps' milestone this Saturday.
